skill/summarize.tagline: Summarize any link, video, or file fast
skill/summarize.overview: Summarize is a command-line tool that turns long content into short summaries. Point it at a web page, a YouTube link, a podcast, an article, a PDF, or a local file and it returns the key points, and it can also pull a best-effort transcript from videos. It is great when you want the gist of something without reading or watching the whole thing.
capabilities: Summarizes URLs, articles, PDFs, and local files
Handles YouTube and other videos, plus podcasts
Extracts a best-effort video transcript with --extract (no yt-dlp needed)
Falls back to a tight summary first when a transcript is huge
Uses your own AI provider key (for example OpenAI)
useCases: A student who was sent a long article or lecture video and wants the main points before class
Anyone who needs a quick transcript of a YouTube talk to quote or study from
Researchers triaging many links to decide which ones are worth a full read
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install steipete/tap/summarize (or use npx skills add to add it as a skill)
Set the API key for your AI provider, e.g. export OPENAI_API_KEY=...
Run summarize followed by a URL, file path, or YouTube link
For a video transcript, add --youtube auto --extract
If a transcript is too long, read the summary first, then ask to expand a specific section
goodToKnow: It needs an API key for a provider like OpenAI, so summaries cost provider tokens.
Video transcripts are best-effort, so accuracy varies by source and may miss parts of long videos.

skill/nano-pdf.overview: nano-pdf is a command-line tool that edits a PDF using a natural-language instruction instead of a PDF editor. You tell it which page to change and describe the edit in words, and it applies the change for you. It is handy for quick text fixes on a slide or document when you do not want to open heavy software.
capabilities: Applies natural-language edits to a chosen PDF page
Fixes typos, swaps titles, and adjusts wording
Works from a single command line, no GUI editor needed
Writes out an edited copy of the PDF
useCases: A student fixing a typo or title on a one-page handout or deck before submitting
Anyone making a quick last-minute text change to a PDF without a full editor
howTo: Install it with uv: uv tool install nano-pdf (or use npx skills add to add it as a skill)
Run nano-pdf edit, then the file, the page number, and your instruction in quotes
If the edited page is off by one, retry using the other page-numbering (0-based vs 1-based)
Open and check the output PDF before sending it out

example.label: Change a title on page 1
example.value: nano-pdf edit deck.pdf 1 "Change the title to 'Q3 Results' and fix the typo in the subtitle"

goodToKnow: Page numbering can be 0-based or 1-based depending on version, so the page you edit may come out off by one.
Always sanity-check the result; AI edits can change layout or wording in unexpected ways.

skill/himalaya.tagline: Manage your email from the terminal
skill/himalaya.overview: Himalaya is a command-line email client that talks to any IMAP/SMTP mailbox. From the shell you can list, read, search, compose, reply, forward, copy, move, and delete messages. It is a fast, keyboard-driven way to handle email without a web interface.
capabilities: Lists folders and message envelopes
Reads and searches mail (for example by sender or subject)
Composes, replies to, and forwards messages
Copies, moves, and deletes messages between folders
Configurable per-account via a TOML config file
useCases: A student who lives in the terminal and wants to triage email without a browser
Scripting or automating email tasks like searching for invoices or filing messages
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install himalaya (or use npx skills add to add it as a skill)
Run himalaya account configure to set up your IMAP/SMTP account
Store credentials in a password manager or keyring, not in plain text
List mail with himalaya envelope list and read one with himalaya message read <id>
Compose, reply, or forward with himalaya message write / reply / forward

example.label: Search mail by sender and subject
example.value: himalaya envelope list from alice@example.com subject invoice

goodToKnow: You must configure IMAP/SMTP details yourself, and a wrong server or port will block sending or reading.
Keep credentials in a keyring; do not paste passwords into chat or logs.

skill/wacli.tagline: WhatsApp messaging and history from the CLI
skill/wacli.overview: wacli is a command-line tool for sending WhatsApp messages and for syncing and searching your WhatsApp history, separate from your live chats. It lets a script or agent send messages and look back through past conversations from the terminal. Use it when you want WhatsApp actions outside the phone or desktop app.
capabilities: Sends third-party WhatsApp messages from the command line
Syncs your WhatsApp message history locally
Searches through synced history
Runs separately from your active WhatsApp chats
useCases: Sending an automated or scripted WhatsApp notification from a workflow
A student searching old WhatsApp threads for a shared link or note without scrolling the app
howTo: Add the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/steipete/clawdis --skill wacli
Link wacli to your WhatsApp account as the tool instructs (typically a one-time pairing)
Sync your history before searching it
Send a message by giving wacli the recipient and the text
goodToKnow: It works separately from your active chats, so treat it as a distinct WhatsApp session.
Automated WhatsApp sending can run against WhatsApp's terms; use it responsibly and avoid spam.

skill/gifgrep.tagline: Search and grab GIFs from the terminal
skill/gifgrep.overview: gifgrep searches GIF providers like Tenor and Giphy from a command line or a terminal UI, downloads results, and can extract a still frame or a contact sheet. It gives you a quick search-preview-download-extract flow for finding and sharing GIFs. Good for grabbing the right reaction GIF without opening a browser.
capabilities: Searches GIF providers (Tenor/Giphy) from CLI or TUI
Downloads results to your Downloads folder
Extracts a still frame or a contact sheet from a GIF
Outputs URLs or JSON for scripting (pipe to jq)
Shows inline previews in Kitty/Ghostty terminals
useCases: Quickly finding a reaction GIF to drop into a chat
A creator pulling a still frame or contact sheet from a GIF for a thumbnail or review
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install steipete/tap/gifgrep (or go install, or npx skills add)
Search with gifgrep <query> --max 5
Browse interactively with gifgrep tui "query"
Add --download to save results, and --reveal to show the file in Finder
Extract a still with gifgrep still ./clip.gif --at 1.5s -o still.png

example.label: Search and download one cat GIF

goodToKnow: Inline thumbnail previews only work in Kitty or Ghostty terminals.
Downloads go to ~/Downloads by default.

skill/sherpa-onnx-tts.overview: sherpa-onnx-tts turns text into spoken audio entirely on your own machine using the sherpa-onnx engine, with no cloud service or API key. You download a runtime and a voice model once, then generate speech files locally. It is a good fit when you want private, offline voice output.
capabilities: Generates spoken audio from text locally
Runs fully offline with no cloud calls
Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows
Uses downloadable Piper/VITS voice models (e.g. en_US lessac)
useCases: A student turning notes or articles into audio to listen to while commuting, without sending text to a cloud
Privacy-conscious or offline use where cloud TTS is not allowed
howTo: Add the skill, which downloads the sherpa-onnx runtime for your OS and a voice model
Set SHERPA_ONNX_RUNTIME_DIR and SHERPA_ONNX_MODEL_DIR to those folders
Provide your text and run the skill to synthesize an audio file
Play back or save the generated audio
goodToKnow: The runtime and voice models are sizable downloads you grab once before first use.
Voice quality depends on the model you download; the bundled Piper voice is English (en_US).

skill/blogwatcher.tagline: Track blogs and RSS feeds for new posts
skill/blogwatcher.overview: blogwatcher is a small command-line tool that monitors blogs and RSS/Atom feeds for new posts. You add the sites you care about, scan for updates, and list or mark articles as read. It is a simple way to keep up with several blogs from one place in the terminal.
capabilities: Adds and removes blogs and RSS/Atom feeds to track
Scans tracked feeds for new posts
Lists new articles
Marks individual articles or all articles as read
useCases: A student following a few research or course blogs who wants one place to see what is new
Keeping a reading queue of feeds without a heavy RSS reader app
howTo: Install it with Go: go install github.com/Hyaxia/blogwatcher/cmd/blogwatcher@latest
Add a blog with blogwatcher add "My Blog" https://example.com
Run blogwatcher scan to check for updates
List new posts with blogwatcher articles and mark them read with blogwatcher read <n>
goodToKnow: Installation is via Go, so you need the Go toolchain on your machine.
It checks for updates when you run scan; it is not a live background daemon.

skill/oracle.tagline: Get a second AI model to review your code
skill/oracle.overview: oracle bundles a prompt plus a set of files you choose and sends them to a second, strong AI model for one review, debug, refactor, or design-critique pass. It can preview the token cost first with a dry run, and run through either a browser session or a direct API call. Treat its output as advice and verify it against your code and tests.
capabilities: Runs a second model over selected files to review, debug, refactor, or critique design
Previews payload and token spend with --dry-run and --files-report
Supports a browser engine (for long ChatGPT Pro runs) or a direct API engine
Lets you reattach to a stored session if a run times out
useCases: A student stuck on a bug who wants a fresh, powerful model to review just the relevant files
Getting a design or refactor critique before committing a tricky change
howTo: Install it with Node: npm install -g @steipete/oracle (or use npx skills add)
Pick the smallest set of files that contains the real problem
Preview cost first with oracle --dry-run summary --files-report
Choose an engine: --engine browser for long Pro runs, or --engine api with OPENAI_API_KEY set
Review the advice against your own code and tests before applying it

example.label: Preview the payload and token spend first

goodToKnow: Output is advisory only; the second model can be confidently wrong, so verify against tests.
API mode needs an OpenAI or Azure key and spends tokens; browser mode needs a ChatGPT session.

skill/openhue.tagline: Control Philips Hue lights from the CLI
skill/openhue.overview: openhue is a command-line tool for controlling Philips Hue lights and scenes through your Hue Bridge. You can turn lights on or off, dim them, set colors or color temperature, and activate scenes. It only works with Philips Hue gear, not other smart-home brands.
capabilities: Turns Hue lights on and off
Adjusts brightness, color, and color temperature
Activates Hue scenes (for example movie mode)
Lists and targets specific lights, rooms, or zones
useCases: Setting the room mood for studying or movie night from the terminal or a script
Automating lights as part of a routine without opening the Hue phone app
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install openhue/cli/openhue-cli (or use npx skills add)
Pair the CLI with your Hue Bridge by following its setup prompt
List your lights and rooms with openhue get light and openhue get room
Turn lights on or off and set brightness or color for a chosen room or light
goodToKnow: It only controls Philips Hue devices; other brands, HomeKit scenes, thermostats, and TVs are not supported.
You need a Hue Bridge on your network and a one-time pairing before commands work.

skill/trello.tagline: Manage Trello boards from the command line
skill/trello.overview: This skill manages Trello boards, lists, and cards directly through the Trello REST API using curl and jq. You set an API key and token, then read boards, lists, and cards or create and update them from the shell. It is useful for scripting Trello tasks without the web app.
capabilities: Lists your boards, lists, and cards
Creates and updates cards via the Trello REST API
Uses curl + jq so output is easy to filter and script
Authenticates with your personal Trello API key and token
useCases: A student automating a study or project board (for example adding cards from a script)
Pulling a quick list of cards in a Trello list without opening the browser
howTo: Get your Trello API key at trello.com/app-key and generate a token
Export TRELLO_API_KEY and TRELLO_TOKEN in your shell
Install jq with brew install jq if you do not have it
Call the Trello REST API with curl and pipe the JSON through jq to read boards, lists, or cards
goodToKnow: Your API key and token grant access to your Trello account, so keep them out of shared logs.
You build requests with raw curl calls, so you need the board, list, or card IDs to act on them.

skill/tmux.overview: This skill controls tmux sessions and panes so you can drive interactive command-line programs: list sessions, capture what is on screen, send keystrokes, paste text, and watch for prompts. It is meant for working with already-running interactive tmux sessions, not one-off commands. It is the go-to when an agent needs to type into a live program like a REPL or a wizard.
capabilities: Lists tmux sessions, windows, and panes
Captures pane output, including scrollback history
Sends literal text and special keys (Ctrl-C, Enter, Escape)
Pastes text into a pane and watches for prompts
useCases: An agent or script that must answer prompts in a live interactive CLI (an installer, a REPL, a TUI)
Capturing the current output of a long-running session to check progress
howTo: Install tmux with brew install tmux if needed (macOS or Linux only)
List sessions with tmux ls and find your target as session:window.pane
Read a pane with tmux capture-pane -t shared:0.0 -p
Send text then Enter with tmux send-keys -t shared:0.0 -l -- "text" and a separate Enter
Send control keys like C-c when you need to interrupt a program

example.label: Capture what is on a pane

goodToKnow: It is for existing interactive sessions; for one-shot commands just use a normal shell.
tmux is macOS/Linux only, and you must target the right session:window.pane or keystrokes go nowhere.

skill/gh-issues.tagline: Turn GitHub issues into pull requests automatically
skill/gh-issues.overview: gh-issues automates the issue-to-PR loop: it fetches GitHub issues, picks candidates, spawns background agents to fix them, and opens pull requests, and it can also work through PR review comments. It uses the gh CLI and can filter issues by label, milestone, assignee, or state. It is built for batching routine fixes across a repo.
capabilities: Fetches and filters issues by label, milestone, assignee, or state
Spawns background agents to attempt fixes and opens PRs
Can push branches to a fork and PR back to the source repo
Processes PR review comments in a reviews-only mode
Supports watch/cron polling and a dry-run listing mode
useCases: A maintainer batching small, well-scoped issues into draft PRs
A student learning a codebase by auto-drafting fixes for labeled good-first-issues
howTo: Install the GitHub CLI with brew install gh and authenticate (set GH_TOKEN)
Run the skill in a repo, or pass owner/repo explicitly
Filter with flags like --label, --milestone, --assignee, or --state
Start with --dry-run to list candidates before any agents run
Use --reviews-only to handle PR review comments instead of fixing issues

example.label: List candidate issues without making changes

goodToKnow: It opens real PRs and runs autonomous agents, so always start with --dry-run and review output.
Auto-generated fixes vary in quality and still need human review before merging.

skill/spotify-player.overview: This skill controls Spotify playback and search from the terminal using spogo (preferred) or spotify_player. You can search tracks, play, pause, skip, pick a playback device, and check status. It needs a Spotify Premium account to control playback.
capabilities: Searches Spotify for tracks
Controls playback: play, pause, next, previous
Lists and selects playback devices
Shows current playback status
Uses spogo by default, falling back to spotify_player
useCases: Starting study or focus music without leaving the terminal
Scripting playback (for example a command that plays a focus playlist)
howTo: Install with Homebrew: brew install steipete/tap/spogo (or brew install spotify_player)
Authenticate spogo with spogo auth import --browser chrome
Search with spogo search track "query"
Control playback with spogo play, pause, next, or prev
Pick a device with spogo device list and spogo device set "<name>"
goodToKnow: Controlling playback requires a Spotify Premium account.
spogo authenticates by importing browser cookies, so you must be logged in to Spotify in that browser.

skill/goplaces.tagline: Query Google Places from the command line
skill/goplaces.overview: goplaces is a CLI for the new Google Places API. You can do text searches, get place details and reviews, resolve a place name to an ID, and output clean JSON for scripts. It needs a Google Places API key and returns human-readable text by default.
capabilities: Text search for places with filters like open-now and minimum rating
Location biasing by latitude, longitude, and radius
Place details including reviews
Resolves a place name or address to candidates
Outputs JSON with --json for scripting
useCases: A student finding a well-rated cafe or study spot near campus, filtered by rating and open-now
Scripting place lookups (for example pulling details and reviews into a JSON file)
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install steipete/tap/goplaces
Set your key: export GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY=...
Search with goplaces search "coffee" --open-now --min-rating 4 --limit 5
Get details and reviews with goplaces details <place_id> --reviews
Add --json when you want machine-readable output

example.label: Search for highly-rated open coffee shops

goodToKnow: It requires a Google Places API key, and the Places API can incur Google charges per request.
The type filter only sends the first --type value because the API accepts one.

skill/openai-whisper.tagline: Transcribe audio locally, no API key
skill/openai-whisper.overview: This skill uses OpenAI's Whisper command-line tool to transcribe speech to text on your own machine, with no API key required. You point it at an audio file and it writes out a transcript, and it can also translate speech into English. Bigger models are more accurate but slower.
capabilities: Transcribes audio files to text locally
Translates speech to English with --task translate
Outputs multiple formats (txt, srt, and more)
Lets you trade speed for accuracy by choosing a model size
Runs offline once models are downloaded
useCases: A student transcribing a recorded lecture or interview without sending audio to the cloud
Generating subtitles (SRT) for a video
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install openai-whisper
Run whisper /path/audio.mp3 --model medium --output_format txt --output_dir .
Add --task translate to get an English transcript from another language
Pick a smaller model for speed or a larger one for accuracy

example.label: Transcribe an audio file to a text file

goodToKnow: Models download to ~/.cache/whisper on first run, which can be a large one-time download.
Larger models are much more accurate but noticeably slower, especially without a GPU.

skill/xurl.tagline: Authenticated X (Twitter) actions from the CLI
skill/xurl.overview: xurl is a command-line tool for authenticated X (Twitter) actions: posting, replies, reads and search, DMs, media upload, follows, and raw X v2 API calls. Shortcut commands return JSON, and a raw mode lets you hit any v2 endpoint. It handles auth so you can script X without writing API boilerplate.
capabilities: Posts, replies to, quotes, and deletes posts
Reads posts and searches X
Shows your timeline, mentions, and user profiles
Uploads media and sends DMs
Makes raw calls to any X v2 API endpoint
useCases: Scripting a post or scheduled update to X from the terminal
Pulling search results or a timeline into JSON for analysis
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install xdevplatform/tap/xurl (or npm i -g @xdevplatform/xurl)
Authenticate, then confirm with xurl auth status
Post with xurl post "Hello world!" or read with xurl read POST_ID
Search with xurl search "query" -n 20
Avoid --verbose in agent sessions and never print the ~/.xurl secrets file
goodToKnow: Auth tokens live in ~/.xurl; never read, print, or share that file, and avoid --verbose which can leak headers.
X API access depends on your developer tier, so some endpoints or rate limits may apply.

skill/blucli.tagline: Control BluOS / Bluesound speakers from the CLI
skill/blucli.overview: blucli (the blu command) controls BluOS-based music players such as Bluesound and NAD from the command line. It handles device discovery, playback, speaker grouping, and volume. You pick a target device and then play, pause, group speakers, or change volume.
capabilities: Discovers BluOS/Bluesound/NAD devices on your network
Controls playback: play, pause, stop
Sets volume and shows status
Groups and ungroups speakers
Searches and plays TuneIn radio; supports --json for scripts
useCases: Starting or pausing music on a Bluesound speaker from the terminal
Grouping multiple speakers for whole-home audio via a script
howTo: Install it with Go: go install github.com/steipete/blucli/cmd/blu@latest
List devices with blu devices and pick your target
Check a device with blu --device <id> status
Control playback with blu play, pause, or stop, and set volume with blu volume set 15
Group speakers with blu group add and confirm the target before changing playback

example.label: List BluOS devices on your network

goodToKnow: It only works with BluOS players (Bluesound/NAD) on your local network.
Confirm the target device first, since commands change playback on real speakers.

skill/gog.tagline: Google Workspace from one command line
skill/gog.overview: gog is a command-line tool for Google Workspace, covering Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Contacts, Sheets, and Docs. After a one-time OAuth setup you can search and send mail, manage calendar events, search Drive, and read or update Sheets and Docs. It puts most of Google Workspace behind one fast CLI.
capabilities: Gmail: search, send, draft, and reply to messages
Calendar: list, create, and update events (with colors)
Drive and Contacts: search files and list contacts
Sheets: read, update, append, and clear ranges
Docs: export and read document contents
useCases: A student searching recent email or sending a quick message from the terminal
Scripting Google Sheets updates or pulling calendar events into a script
howTo: Install it with Homebrew: brew install gogcli
Set up OAuth once: gog auth credentials /path/to/client_secret.json
Add your account: gog auth add you@gmail.com --services gmail,calendar,drive,contacts,docs,sheets
Search mail with gog gmail search 'newer_than:7d' --max 10
Read or update a sheet with gog sheets get / gog sheets update
goodToKnow: It needs a one-time Google OAuth setup with your own client_secret.json before anything works.
It has broad access to your Google account, so review what services you grant during auth.

skill/things-mac.tagline: Control Things 3 to-dos from the terminal
skill/things-mac.overview: things-mac (the things command) reads your local Things 3 database and adds or updates to-dos via the Things URL scheme on macOS. You can view inbox, today, and upcoming, search tasks, list projects, areas, and tags, and create or edit to-dos. It is a fast terminal front-end for Things 3.
capabilities: Reads inbox, today, and upcoming tasks
Searches tasks and lists projects, areas, and tags
Adds to-dos with notes, dates, tags, lists, and checklists
Updates existing to-dos (requires an auth token)
Supports a --dry-run preview before writing
useCases: A student quickly capturing a task into Things without switching apps
Reviewing today's or upcoming to-dos from the terminal
howTo: Install it with Go: GOBIN=/opt/homebrew/bin go install github.com/ossianhempel/things3-cli/cmd/things@latest
If database reads fail, grant Full Disk Access to your terminal app
View tasks with things today or things inbox --limit 50
Add a task with things add "Title" --notes "..." --when today
For updates, set THINGS_AUTH_TOKEN and edit by the task's UUID

example.label: Add a to-do with notes and a due date

goodToKnow: macOS only, and reading the database may require granting Full Disk Access.
Updating existing to-dos needs an auth token; preview risky writes with --dry-run first.

skill/1password.tagline: Read and inject secrets with 1Password CLI
skill/1password.overview: This skill sets up and uses the 1Password CLI (op) to sign in, integrate with the 1Password desktop app, and read or inject secrets into commands. It detects your auth mode (service account, desktop app, or standalone sign-in) and runs op accordingly. It lets scripts use secrets without hardcoding them.
capabilities: Signs in to 1Password from the CLI across auth modes
Reads individual secrets with op read using secret references
Lists vaults and verifies access with op whoami
Integrates with the desktop app (Touch ID / system auth)
Supports service-account tokens for headless/CI use
useCases: A developer injecting an API key into a command without writing it into a script
Headless or CI setups that need secrets via a 1Password service account
howTo: Install the CLI with Homebrew: brew install 1password-cli
Verify it is present with op --version
Pick your auth mode: service-account token, desktop app integration, or standalone op signin
Confirm access with op whoami before reading anything
Read a secret with op read using an op:// reference
goodToKnow: Follow 1Password's official setup steps rather than guessing install commands.
Run op directly (not inside tmux) for desktop-app integration, since the IPC channel may not reach tmux subshells.
